title: 中国軍大混乱が強いる拙速な習近平・鄭麗文会談、台湾軍事侵攻の虚実
extracted_text:
台湾の最大野党・国民党の女性主席（党首）である鄭麗文は178センチメートルと高身長で、長い黒髪が特徴。56歳である。10日、北京の人民大会堂で中国共産党総書記、習近平（シー・ジンピン、72）と握手した際、見た目がさらに大きくなる高いヒール付きの靴は履いていなかった。

それでも180センチメートルほどとされるがっしりした体軀（たいく）の中国トップ、習と並んで、ほぼ同じ身長。全く遜色ない。見方によっては、鄭麗文のほうが堂々としている。

今回の会談前、2人の握手を撮影する場所に先に入って鄭麗文を待ったのは習だった。入場の際には、カメラを構える多くの鄭麗文の同行記者らに親しげに声までかけた。「おお。けっこう多くの記者が来ているね」。異様な愛想のよさは想定外。突出している。これは「ある種の譲歩」といってよい。

今、中国共産党の習側近らが最も気にするのは習のメンツのはずだ。権力集中に成功し、別格の地位を持つ権力者として威厳を保つ必要がある。鄭麗文は国民党トップであっても、台湾政治を仕切る政権与党のトップではない。習が2015年、シンガポールで対等な立場で会った当時の台湾総統、馬英九との歴史的な長い握手とは全く異なる。

鄭麗文は若い頃、中国が「独立勢力」とする現在の台湾の与党、民主進歩党（民進党）に在籍した経歴がある。その後、主張、立場を変えて国民党に移った「転向組」なのだ。

これは習政権がトップ会談を決断する際、大きなマイナス材料で、慎重に検討すべき案件のはずだった。しかも鄭麗文はトップ就任後、日が浅く、実績もない。28年の次期台湾総統選で国民党の総統候補になるにも壁がある。他に有力候補がいるのだ。

それでも中国側は、鄭麗文を早々に北京に呼ぶ賭けに出た。2人の握手は14秒という異例の長さ。同格感が出る構図で習との写真も撮らせた。こうした「ある種の譲歩」の裏には、中国側の深謀があるはずだ。

「一見、関連性がない（中国）軍の大混乱と、拙速すぎる習・鄭麗文会談の2つはつながっている。実は裏と表の関係にあるのだ」。中台問題に精通する関係者はこう解説する。

中国軍の異常さを明確に示すニュース映像がある。習・鄭麗文の会談の2日前、北京の国防大学で開かれた全軍の高級幹部を対象とした研修の開始式だ。正面の舞台上の長机には2人しかいない。中央には軍トップの中央軍事委員会主席である習が座る。これは当然だ。

右の席には同副主席の張昇民がいる。だが、左側に延びた机には椅子もなく、ただ空いているだけ。名札も中央と右にしかない。バランスが全く取れない居心地の悪い配置である。当初7人いた中央軍事委メンバーが軒並み粛清された結果だ。

舞台上の習が発する演説を聞く軍高級幹部らの顔ぶれをみると、つい最近までいた最高階級の上将らが軒並み消えている。各軍の現場指揮官である司令員、政治委員らだ。既に粛清されたか、行方不明なのだ。

代わりとなる下級の将官は既にいる。それでも統率がとれた指揮をするにはそれなりの訓練、現場経験が必要だ。今、直ちに台湾に武力侵攻できる体制を整えるのは容易ではない。

封鎖戦術などは可能としても、上陸・侵攻のハードルは極めて高い。いわゆる武力統一に一気に踏み出すのは非現実的で、リスクが高すぎる。今回の米軍のイラン攻撃では、米中間に軍事技術を巡る巨大な格差があることも浮き彫りになった。習と中国軍は衝撃を受けたはずである。

時系列を思い起こすと、興味深い事実が浮かび上がる。ダークホースといえる鄭麗文が国民党主席に選ばれたのは25年10月18日だ。その前日だった17日、中国国防省は、中国軍の軍事行動に関して最終決定権を持つ中央軍事委の副主席、何衛東ら幹部9人について、党籍と軍籍の剝奪を発表した。

同19日になると、習は国民党主席に当選したばかりの鄭麗文に祝電を送る。そして、同20日には中国共産党の重要会議、中央委員会第4回全体会議（4中全会）が北京で開幕する。中国軍粛清が最大の政治課題だった会議である。

ちなみに同じ10月、日本でも政局が動いていた。政権与党、自民党の総裁に高市早苗が選ばれ、女性として初の首相に指名された。だが、習は、その高市には祝電さえ送っていない。

つまり、25年10月、中国共産党は軍を巡る苛烈な権力闘争のまっただ中にいた。台湾に直ちに軍事侵攻できるような状態ではない。その間に台湾の国民党では、明確に親中といえる鄭麗文がトップに選ばれた。意外な結果だが、好機でもある。乗らない手はない。

拙速であっても鄭麗文を利用しながら時間を稼ぐ。その判断は当然だった。中台の平和統一という中国側の夢はなお絶たれていない。それが将来、実現する可能性は十分に残っている。そう内外にアピールするには、習・鄭麗文会談が有効だ。

今年に入ると中国軍内には、さらに大きな衝撃が走る。1月24日、習のかつての盟友で軍制服組トップの張又俠が「調査」の対象となったと突然発表され、失脚した。この頃、習政権は鄭麗文の北京への招待という大きな決断を既に下していた。中国軍混乱と鄭麗文訪中の調整という2つの問題は同時進行していた。

当初、3月末に予定していた米大統領のトランプ訪中は、2月末に米軍によるイラン攻撃が始まったため、5月中旬に延期された。その結果、鄭麗文の北京入りは、それに先立つ4月になった。

米軍のイラン攻撃は今回の習・鄭麗文会談にも影響した。大イベントは国際的には埋もれてしまった感が強い。世界が注視したパキスタンを舞台にした米・イラン停戦協議を巡る国際的な報道合戦とぴったり時間的に重なり、その裏に隠れてしまったのだ。

それでも習政権にとって台湾の一部勢力との融和ムード演出、「一つの中国」を巡る「1992年コンセンサス」への言及は重要だった。中国軍の混乱を完全に収拾し、体制を組み直すには一定の時間が必要だからである。注目を集めてきた中国軍による台湾への直接的な軍事侵攻。短期的な時間感覚でいえば、そこには虚実が入り交じっている。（敬称略）

translated_text:
Cheng Li-wen, the female chairman of Taiwan's largest opposition party the Kuomintang, is tall at 178 centimeters with long black hair as her defining feature. She is 56 years old. On the 10th, when she shook hands with Chinese Communist Party General Secretary Xi Jinping (72) at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, she was not wearing high-heeled shoes that would have made her appear even taller.

Nevertheless, standing alongside China's leader Xi, whose sturdy frame is said to be around 180 centimeters, they were nearly the same height. There was no difference at all. Depending on how you look at it, Cheng Li-wen appeared even more dignified.

Before this meeting, Xi was the one who entered first and waited for Cheng Li-wen at the spot where their handshake would be photographed. Upon entering, he even warmly greeted the many accompanying journalists from Cheng Li-wen's press corps who were readying their cameras. "Oh, quite a lot of journalists have come." This unusual friendliness was unexpected and stood out. It can be described as "a certain concession."

What Xi Jinping's closest allies in the Chinese Communist Party are most concerned about now should be Xi's face. Having succeeded in consolidating power, he needs to maintain his authority as a power holder with a special status. Even though Cheng Li-wen is the KMT leader, she is not the leader of the ruling party that controls Taiwanese politics. This is completely different from the historic long handshake Xi had in 2015 in Singapore with then-Taiwan President Ma Ying-jeou, whom he met on equal terms.

When she was younger, Cheng Li-wen was a member of Taiwan's current ruling party, the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP), which China labels as an "independence force." She later changed her views and position and transferred to the KMT, becoming part of the "turncoat group."

This should have been a major negative factor for the Xi administration when deciding on the top-level meeting, something that should have been carefully considered. Moreover, Cheng Li-wen has been in her leadership position for a short time with no track record. There are also barriers for her to become the KMT's presidential candidate in the next Taiwan presidential election in 2028. There are other strong candidates.

Nevertheless, the Chinese side took the gamble of summoning Cheng Li-wen to Beijing early on. Their handshake lasted an unusually long 14 seconds. They also had photos taken with Xi in compositions that conveyed a sense of equality. Behind this "certain concession," there must be deep calculation on the Chinese side.

"At first glance, the two seemingly unrelated matters—the major chaos in the (Chinese) military and the overly hasty Xi-Cheng Li-wen meeting—are connected. In fact, they are two sides of the same coin." So explained an expert familiar with Taiwan-China issues.

There is video news footage that clearly shows the abnormality in the Chinese military. Two days before the Xi-Cheng meeting, a training opening ceremony for senior military officials from all branches was held at the National Defense University in Beijing. On the long table on the stage at the front, there were only two people. Naturally, at the center sat Xi, who is the chairman of the Central Military Commission, the top of the military.

On the right seat was Vice Chairman Zhang Shengmin. However, the table extending to the left side had no chairs and was simply empty. Name plates existed only at the center and right. The layout was completely unbalanced and uncomfortable. This was the result of the seven original Central Military Commission members being purged one after another.

Looking at the faces of the senior military officials listening to Xi's speech on the stage, all the highest-ranked generals who were there until recently have disappeared—the commanders and political commissars of the various military branches. They have either already been purged or are missing in action.

There are already junior generals to replace them. However, they need considerable training and field experience to command with cohesion. It is not easy to immediately prepare for a military invasion of Taiwan.

While blockade tactics may be possible, the hurdles for landing and invasion are extremely high. It is unrealistic and too risky to suddenly pursue so-called military unification. The recent U.S. attack on Iran also highlighted the enormous gap in military technology between the U.S. and China. Xi and the Chinese military must have been shocked.

When reviewing the timeline, interesting facts come to light. Cheng Li-wen, who can be considered a dark horse, was elected KMT chairman on October 18, 2025. The day before, on the 17th, China's Ministry of Defense announced the removal of party and military membership for nine military officials including Central Military Commission Vice Chairman He Weidong and other cadres who hold final decision-making authority over Chinese military operations.

Then on the 19th, Xi sent a congratulatory telegram to Cheng Li-wen, who had just been elected KMT chairman. And on the 20th, the important Chinese Communist Party meeting, the Fourth Plenary Session of the Central Committee (4th Plenum), opened in Beijing. The Chinese military purge was the biggest political agenda at that meeting.

By the way, in the same October, political developments were also happening in Japan. Ishiba Sanae was elected president of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party and became the first female prime minister. However, Xi did not even send a congratulatory telegram to Ishiba.

In other words, in October 2025, the Chinese Communist Party was in the midst of a fierce power struggle regarding the military. It was not in a state where it could immediately launch a military invasion of Taiwan. During that time, in Taiwan's KMT, Cheng Li-wen, clearly pro-China, was elected leader. It was an unexpected result but also an opportunity. It would be foolish not to take it.

Even if hasty, the judgment to use Cheng Li-wen to buy time was natural. The Chinese side's dream of peaceful unification across the Taiwan Strait has not been completely extinguished. There is still ample possibility of it being realized in the future. To promote this both domestically and internationally, the Xi-Cheng Li-wen meeting was effective.

Since the start of this year, there has been even greater shock within the Chinese military. On January 24, it was suddenly announced that Zhang Youxian, once Xi's ally and the top uniformed military official, became the subject of an "investigation" and fell from power. By this time, the Xi administration had already made the major decision to invite Cheng Li-wen to Beijing. The two issues—the Chinese military chaos and the Cheng Li-wen visit arrangement—were proceeding simultaneously.

The U.S. President Trump's visit to China, originally scheduled for late March, was postponed to mid-May because the U.S. military attack on Iran began at the end of February. As a result, Cheng Li-wen's arrival in Beijing was moved to April, prior to that.

The U.S. military attack on Iran also affected the Xi-Cheng Li-wen meeting. The major event somewhat got lost in the international shuffle. It coincided exactly with the time of international media coverage surrounding the U.S.-Iran ceasefire talks in Pakistan that the world was watching, and it was overshadowed.

Nevertheless, for the Xi administration, creating a conciliatory atmosphere with certain Taiwanese factions and referencing the "1992 Consensus" regarding "one China" was important. This is because completely resolving the Chinese military chaos and restructuring the system will require a considerable amount of time. The direct military invasion of Taiwan by the Chinese military, which has attracted attention, involves a mix of truth and fiction from a short-term perspective.
title_en: Chinese Military Chaos Forced Hasty Xi-Cheng Li-wen Meeting, Truth and Fiction of Taiwan Military Invasion
